title: I wanted to test if AI can be the director of a game, and it turned into a whole engine
author: IfnotFr
selftext:
I have been working as a developer for 10+ years and I am used to building everything by hand: backend, servers, load systems. But when I started experimenting with LLM I wanted to give it more freedom. Not just to answer questions or chat, but to control the storyline of a game in real time.

My first experiment was simple: AI had to create a room, two characters and a dialogue between them. I thought it would break on the second line. But the story kept going. Then I allowed the player to intervene in the scene and AI picked up the choice, changing the development of events.

From this chaotic prototype grew Dream Novel - an engine that generates visual novels. There is no scripted plot, you act and the game writes the continuation itself. Scenes, characters, dialogues, everything is born during the game.

I am now at the beta testing stage, and I want to understand how interesting this approach can be for this community. This is an experiment with a new format. Can AI become not just a tool, but a full-fledged co-creator of a game?

If you’re interested in trying it out, the open beta is live here: https://dream-novel.com/

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
Curious what LLM's you are using on the backend for this, and do you use different ones for the image generation versus text generation?

Also the site does not describe super well where this runs. Is this meant for a web application with webgl or does this run as a native app on Windows or Mac?

replies.author: IfnotFr
replies.body:
Honestly, it’s running in my living room on a mining rig adapted into an AI cluster :’)

I mainly use cloud models for “creativity” (grok, mistral, gemini). For classification, embeddings, the agent, and tool calling, I’m running everything locally on my rig in the living room.

I’m still at the prototype stage, so nothing is final yet, and I’m considering a fully local Steam version for powerful gaming PCs!

replies.body:
Thank fuck you didn’t give your real email, I don’t want to pay for cloud credits for you for free.

Sorry, I’m not a big company that can hand out freebies to everyone.

replies.author: mspaintshoops
replies.body: And yet you’re not up-front about your pricing model or even what this service really is. Not shady at all.

replies.author: IfnotFr
replies.body: There’s no pricing model yet, it’s all free to test and give feedback. It’s just a proof of concept, nothing for sale, just ideas and fun. If it’s not your thing, feel free to move on :-)

replies.author: Careful_Coconut_549
replies.body:
I was maybe a bit snippy. The address Google asked to authenticate on your site with looked shady so I didn't wanna do that & you didn't mention a wait list here so I ended up becoming suspicious of what exactly this is to begin with.


All the best with your project.

replies.body: No hard feelings, yes, the social auth domain uses Supabase’s free, turnkey auth system. I’ll improve that (and pay for Supabase) and use my domain eventually.

comments.body: So you used AI to create an AI chat bot the writers stories? Got it!

comments.author: forShizAndGigz00001
comments.body:
I did this for fun to create an AI dnd game, worked great, had a LLM DM, an LLM for each character and a coordinator LLM for keeping things summarised and flowing correctly.

The whole thing used scene images generated from another llm with input from the coordinator and voices were generated and lip syned to the scene.

Super interesting to build as a learning exercise.

Link for the curious: https://youtu.be/obA5cIufjTM?si=X-rQKAb2U_pQIZhI

comments.body: Looks very cool. I will definitely try it out. I am actually also working on a similar project. Feel free to hit me up for a demo or if you want to compare notes.

comments.author: Syzygy___
comments.body: Do you still have story nodes in the engine, so that a developer can at least define the general outline and the AI handles the inbetween?

comments.author: IdonGames
comments.body: Very impressive but thankfully, this does not mean that AI can make games. Humans still are the only ones capable of putting together a beautiful symphony of mechanics, visuals, audios, systems, story to create meaningful pieces of art that reflect what’s deeper.
